package_info.why_malicious: The packages are considered malicious because they enable unauthorized cryptojacking by downloading and executing remote cryptomining scripts, resulting in resource abuse and unauthorized code execution on victim machines. This activity is performed without user knowledge or consent, violating user trust and system integrity.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the main module is loaded or executed)
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript file of the npm package (e.g., index.js or main entrypoint as defined in package.json)
required_permissions: filesystem (to write/read temporary files or miner payloads)
network (to download remote scripts and communicate with mining pools)
process (to spawn child processes for mining operations)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses child_process.exec to download a remote shell script from http://malicious-domain.com/miner.sh and executes it via bash, resulting in the launch of a cryptominer process that consumes system resources for unauthorized cryptocurrency mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code programmatically downloads and executes a remote shell script from an untrusted domain without user interaction, a hallmark of malware delivery and execution. This behavior is commonly used to deploy cryptominers or other payloads covertly.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not download and execute remote code, especially from untrusted sources, without explicit user consent and transparency. Executing shell commands to run external scripts is outside the expected behavior for most packages.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers or updaters may fetch and execute remote scripts, but only with clear user notification, consent, and from trusted, verifiable sources.
key_indicators: Use of child_process.exec or similar APIs to run shell commands
Fetching and executing code from external, non-trusted domains (e.g., http://malicious-domain.com)
No user interaction or consent required for code execution
Presence of commands that download and pipe scripts directly to bash/sh

attack_chain.action: User installs or runs the malicious npm package, triggering execution of the main module.
attack_chain.leads_to: The package's main JavaScript file is loaded, initiating the malicious code.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads and executes a remote shell script containing the cryptominer.
attack_chain.leads_to: The cryptominer process runs on the victim's machine, consuming CPU and network resources to mine cryptocurrency for the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: npm package executing shell commands at runtime using child_process.exec or spawn
Downloading and executing remote scripts from non-standard or suspicious domains
Unexpected process creation related to known cryptominer binaries (e.g., xmrig, miner.sh)
file_indicators: JavaScript files (e.g., index.js) containing child_process.exec or spawn with remote URLs
Presence of miner.sh or similar shell scripts in temporary or user directories
References to external mining binaries or scripts within package files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to suspicious or non-standard domains (e.g., http://malicious-domain.com/miner.sh)
Connections to known cryptocurrency mining pools or mining-related IP addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations and runtime behavior for unexpected process creation, especially those that download and execute remote scripts using child_process APIs. Flag packages that reference external URLs in exec/spawn commands. Use static analysis to identify code patterns that fetch and execute remote scripts. Network monitoring should alert on outbound connections to suspicious domains or known mining pools. Correlate file system changes for the presence of miner scripts or binaries.
